title: test_dispatch_does_not_block: stop failing under gate load (0.54 s and 1.24 s against a 0.5 s bound)
spec:
Evidence 2026-10-07: tests/test_daemon.py Daemon.test_dispatch_does_not_block failed the gates of T-1707 (1.24 s) and
T-1706 (0.54 s, a task that does not touch daemon.py) while two full gates ran in parallel; it passed 3/3 alone. A wall-clock
bound that tight turns machine load into red gates.
Fix the test, not the daemon: assert the property it guards (dispatch returns before the spawned worker finishes) with a
synchronisation primitive, e.g. the fake worker blocks on a threading.Event that the test sets only after dispatch returned,
and a generous timeout (10 s) only as a hang guard. No change to orchestrator/daemon.py.
Run: PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon.Daemon.test_dispatch_does_not_block 20 times in a loop
while another test_daemon run is in progress; all pass. Commit on the task branch.
acceptance: test_dispatch_does_not_block asserts ordering with an Event, not a 0.5 s wall-clock bound
20 consecutive runs under parallel load pass
